title: Meet the billionaires of the new cloud boom
summary: The growth in cloud software has created a new wave of billionaires, with founders of companies like Atlassian, Zoom, Shopify, and Dropbox amassing significant wealth. This trend highlights investors' interest in "land and expand" business models and recurring revenue, making cloud software a fertile ground for new tech giants. While Salesforce's Marc Benioff was once the dominant figure, many new billionaires now rival or exceed his net worth in the cloud industry.

title: Blackstone to buy warehouse network in record $18.7 billion deal
summary: Blackstone Group LP is set to acquire a network of U.S. industrial warehouses from Singapore-based GLP for a record-breaking $18.7 billion, including debt. This deal marks the largest private real-estate transaction ever and highlights the growing interest in warehouse properties fueled by e-commerce expansion. Blackstone outbid Prologis Inc. for the portfolio, which comprises approximately 180 million square feet of space.

title: Elon Musk Reveals Tesla Pickup Truck's Price: ‘Well Under $50,000’
summary: Elon Musk has revealed the anticipated price point for Tesla's upcoming electric pickup truck, stating it will be "well under $50,000," possibly starting at $49,000. This pricing strategy aims to challenge rivals like Rivian's R1T, which has a higher price tag, and target a broader demographic. Musk also detailed some expected features, including high towing capacity, long range, and advanced technology, positioning it against traditional pickups and sports cars.

title: Blackstone bets big on Amazon, e-commerce with $18.7-billion acquisition
summary: Blackstone Group is making an $18.7-billion acquisition of 179 million square feet of urban logistics properties from Singapore's GLP, significantly expanding its U.S. industrial footprint. This move capitalizes on the increasing demand for warehouse space driven by the growth of Amazon and other e-commerce companies, with properties concentrated in high-growth metropolitan areas. The deal highlights a significant investment trend towards logistics real estate as online shopping continues to reshape retail.

title: Walmart CEO Calls for Raising the Federal Minimum Wage
summary: Walmart CEO Doug McMillon has called for Congress to raise the federal minimum wage, stating the current $7.25 is "too low" and that a thoughtful plan should be put in place. This marks the first time in over a decade a Walmart CEO has specifically demanded new legislation on the matter, despite the company having raised its own starting wage to $11 an hour. The announcement coincided with Senator Bernie Sanders campaigning at Walmart's annual meeting, advocating for a $15 an hour living wage for Walmart workers.

title: Jamie Dimon shows the JPMorgan Chase flag at Philly’s big BIO meeting
summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon spoke at the BIO 2019 conference in Philadelphia, expressing concerns about the "self-inflicted" U.S.-China trade war and the potential for a broader "economic war." He also discussed his company's expansion in Philadelphia, efforts to cut healthcare costs, and the importance of immigration reform and higher minimum wages. Dimon touched on the soundness of the U.S. financial system despite problematic government policies and the need for stronger leadership and tougher journalists.

title: How International Is Your Foreign-Stock Fund?
summary: This article examines the true international exposure of foreign-equity funds by analyzing revenue streams by region rather than traditional business country allocation. It reveals hidden U.S. and emerging-markets exposures in several large foreign stock funds, highlighting how relying solely on a company's headquarters can misrepresent a fund's geographical diversification. The piece uses Morningstar's Revenue Exposure by Region dataset to offer a more nuanced understanding for investors assessing diversification benefits.

title: Commentary: Why Upwork Scratched College Degree Requirements From Our Job Descriptions
summary: Upwork CEO Stephane Kasriel explains why the company removed college degree requirements for all positions. He argues that the rising cost of tuition and the failure of traditional education to keep pace with job market changes are creating a talent gap. The article suggests that businesses should look for alternative ways to identify skilled workers, such as vocational training and apprenticeships, which are more inclusive and relevant to current industry needs.

title: Amazon unveils a chopper-plane mashup to deliver packages
summary: Amazon unveiled a new drone design for its Prime Air fleet, a hybrid helicopter-plane mashup designed for package delivery. The drone features AI and takes off vertically before flying horizontally like a plane. Amazon aims to use these drones for test deliveries of household goods, with the goal of delivering packages within 7.5 miles of a warehouse within 30 minutes, handling items up to five pounds.

title: The Garmin® DriveSmart 65 with Amazon Alexa brings the ultimate voice-controlled navigator to the 2019 Drive series
summary: Garmin International announced the Garmin DriveSmart 65 with Amazon Alexa, a voice-controlled portable navigator. This device integrates Alexa functionality for navigation, music, news, and tasks, enabling hands-free use and maintaining driver focus. It also offers smart notifications, real-time traffic, weather, parking details, and map updates.

title: Amazon CEO confronted by protester in Las Vegas
summary: Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos was confronted by an animal rights activist, Priya Sawhney, during a conference in Las Vegas. Sawhney, identified by Direct Action Everywhere, was protesting conditions at a California poultry farm that supplies Amazon. The incident highlights the company's security spending, which according to Bloomberg News, is about $1.6 million annually for Bezos.

title: Keep an Eye on Hybrid Cloud Computing Trend
summary: The Global X Cloud Computing ETF (CLOU), launched less than two months ago, has already attracted $300 million in assets, indicating strong investor interest in cloud computing. The article suggests that CLOU is well-positioned to capitalize on the emerging hybrid cloud trend, which allows businesses to merge public cloud services with their private data centers. Hybrid cloud computing is projected to become a significant market, with estimates valuing it at up to $63 billion.

title: Scars finally healing decade after Garner ConAgra plant explosion
summary: A decade after a deadly explosion at the ConAgra Foods Inc. plant in Garner killed four people, the community is moving forward with the site now home to a new Amazon distribution center. The 2009 blast, caused by a natural gas leak, led to the plant's eventual closure, but the town of Garner turned the tragedy into an opportunity for economic growth. The article reflects on the immediate aftermath, the plant's closure, and the subsequent redevelopment of the site, marking a healing process for the town.

title: Amazon launches a credit card for the 'underbanked' with bad credit
summary: Amazon, in partnership with Synchrony Financial, has launched "Amazon Credit Builder," a secured credit card program aimed at individuals with no credit history or bad credit. This initiative offers the same 5% cash back perks as the popular Amazon Store card and includes financial literacy tools, allowing users to build credit and eventually "graduate" to an unsecured card. The program addresses a significant market segment of underbanked Americans and comes with a 28.24% APR for the starter card.

title: Synchrony launches Amazon-branded credit card
summary: Synchrony and Amazon have launched a private-label credit card, Amazon Credit Builder, aimed at consumers looking to improve their credit. This no-annual-fee card offers benefits like 5 percent back on purchases for eligible Amazon Prime members and various financing options. The new partnership helps Synchrony offset business lost from Walmart and contributes to its goal of becoming a major digital-payments player.

title: Amazon launches co-branded credit card with Synchrony for the underbanked
summary: Amazon has partnered with Synchrony Financial to launch the Amazon Credit Builder, a co-branded credit card designed for underbanked consumers. This secured card offers similar benefits to Amazon's existing co-branded card, including 5% cashback for eligible Amazon Prime members, and allows cardholders to build credit with an initial deposit ranging from $100 to $1,000. Cardholders can qualify for a regular card after demonstrating responsible payment behavior, with reviews for upgrade starting as soon as seven months after account opening.

title: Target boosts worker benefits, including paid family leave
summary: Target Corp. announced a series of expanded benefits for its full- and part-time workers, including paid family leave and emergency child care, to attract and retain employees in a competitive labor market. The new policies include doubling paid leave to four weeks, extending subsidized backup care to all employees, and increasing adoption and surrogacy reimbursement to $10,000. These moves reflect a broader retail trend of enhancing wages and perks to address workforce challenges like turnover and absenteeism.

title: AWS Recognizes SAIC as ‘Premier’ Consulting Partner; Dave Levy Quoted
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) has recognized Science Applications International Corp. (SAIC) as a "premier" consulting partner under the AWS Partner Network. This top-tier designation acknowledges SAIC's efforts in assisting customers with cloud computing technology. David Levy, VP of the U.S. government business at AWS, expressed excitement about helping government customers achieve their missions faster and more securely through this partnership.

title: FedEx opt out of Express contract with Amazon may be good thing, analysts say
summary: Analysts believe FedEx's decision not to renew its U.S. domestic Express contract with Amazon.com is a positive move for the delivery service company in the long term, despite potential short-term challenges. This move allows FedEx to widen its focus on e-commerce growth across the broader retail sector. Moody's senior vice president Jonathan Root supports this decision, emphasizing the strong e-commerce growth expectations.

title: FedEx opt out of Express contract with Amazon may be good thing, analysts say
summary: Analysts believe FedEx's decision not to renew its Express U.S. domestic contract with Amazon.com Inc. will benefit the delivery service company in the long run. Jonathan Root, Moody’s senior vice president and lead FedEx analyst, stated that this move makes perfect sense given the strong e-commerce growth expectations across the retail sector. FedEx aims to widen its e-commerce focus, despite Amazon representing only a small portion of its Express U.S. domestic business.

title: Amazon Prime Restaurants to shut down restaurant food delivery service in U.S.
summary: Amazon is discontinuing its 4-year-old U.S. restaurant delivery service, Amazon Restaurants, on June 24th due to fierce competition and a small market share. Despite this closure, Amazon recently invested in British food delivery company Deliveroo, suggesting it may not be entirely abandoning the food delivery sector. The news of Amazon's exit caused shares of competitors like Grubhub Inc. to increase by 7%.

title: Amazon Is Shutting Down Its Restaurant Delivery Service In The U.S.
summary: Amazon is shutting down its restaurant delivery service in the U.S. after four years due to intense competition from rivals like Uber Eats and DoorDash. The service, Amazon Restaurants, previously operated in over 20 U.S. cities and expanded to the UK before being closed there last year. Despite this closure, Amazon still shows interest in meal delivery, as evidenced by its recent investment in British food delivery company Deliveroo.

title: Jeff Bezos’ Amazon unveils a credit card for people with no credit history or bad credit
summary: Amazon has launched a new credit card in partnership with Synchrony Financial, called Amazon Credit Builder, aimed at individuals with no credit history or bad credit. The card has an annual percentage rate (APR) of 28.24% and requires users to deposit an equal amount of money for equivalent credit, helping them build a positive credit history to eventually qualify for an unsecured Amazon credit card. This initiative seeks to provide credit facilities to an underserved population.

title: Kohl's adds adaptive clothing to its three top kids' brands
summary: Kohl's has launched a new line of adaptive clothing for children across its three largest kids' brands: Jumping Beans, SO, and Urban Pipeline. This move makes Kohl's one of the largest retailers to enter the growing adaptive clothing market, estimated to reach nearly $289 billion globally this year. The adaptive apparel, designed for easier wear by children with disabilities, aims to boost confidence and independence, offering features like magnetic closures, tagless designs, and softer materials.

title: PetSmart's Chewy gets Wall Street tails wagging with $1 billion IPO
summary: Chewy Inc. priced its initial public offering at $22 per share, exceeding its target and valuing the online pet products retailer at $8.77 billion. The IPO generated funds to help PetSmart manage its debt, demonstrating investor interest in the rapidly growing, albeit loss-making, e-commerce company within the substantial U.S. pet industry. Chewy's sales have surged from $26 million in 2012 to $3.5 billion in 2018, with its net losses narrowing significantly.

title: Chewy raises $1 billion in IPO, and stock soars in trading debut
summary: Chewy Inc. had a successful trading debut after raising $1.02 billion in its initial public offering, with shares soaring by as much as 88% and closing up 59%. The company, backed by PetSmart, plans to expand its private-label products and health services, including prescription drugs, leveraging the consistent growth in pet spending even during economic downturns. This IPO provides significant financial relief for PetSmart, which is burdened with over $8 billion in debt.

title: Tech titans fuel a scramble to build large-scale offices
summary: Tech giants like Google, Amazon, and Netflix are driving a massive scramble for office space in Los Angeles, leading to billions of dollars in new construction and radical redevelopments. These "content creators" prefer large-scale, campus-like facilities with unique amenities over traditional high-rise offices, focusing their hubs in areas like Hollywood, Culver City, and Playa Vista. This trend is sparking an economic boom and attracting a multiplier effect of smaller service providers looking to be near these major players.

title: Domino’s Pizza plans robot deliveries with self-driving minivans in 2019
summary: Domino's Pizza is partnering with Nuro to begin robot deliveries using self-driving R1 minivans in Houston later in 2019. This trial builds on Nuro's previous autonomous grocery deliveries and Domino's ongoing efforts to integrate robotic solutions into its delivery operations, with the R1 vehicles operating on public streets without a human operator. Customers in a designated Houston store will receive a PIN to access their pizza from the self-driving van.

title: Ant Financial's Ability to Disrupt Could Boost EMQQ ETF
summary: The article discusses how Ant Financial's disruptive capabilities, particularly in fintech and now healthcare, could benefit the Emerging Markets Internet & Ecommerce ETF (EMQQ). EMQQ holds Alibaba Group, a majority stakeholder in Ant Financial, positioning the ETF to capitalize on Ant Financial's innovative strategies in emerging markets. The piece highlights the rapid growth in the financial technology space and Ant Financial's expansion into health insurance with its Ziang Hu Bao program, attracting millions of participants.

title: JBG Smith accused of not honoring housing vouchers in Shaw
summary: JBG Smith is accused of not honoring housing vouchers at its Atlantic Plumbing apartments in Shaw, Washington D.C. Resident Regina Williams claims she was denied housing because the property allegedly does not accept vouchers. This accusation comes despite JBG Smith's own initiatives to support affordable housing.

title: Amazon pulls back from original kids programming
summary: Amazon Studios is reportedly scaling back its investment in original animated shows for young children, shifting its focus to content for families to view together and for young adult audiences. This strategic change comes amidst executive changes and internal debates over the value of kids' programming in driving Prime memberships, especially as competitors like Netflix, Disney, and Apple continue to invest heavily in the children's content space. The company will continue to produce existing kids' animated series but will prioritize licensing kids' content and developing more mature animation, including young adult animated series.

title: CIO Hall Of Famer Harry Moseley Puts Zoom On Track To Scale
summary: Harry Moseley, a CIO Hall of Famer, came out of retirement to become Zoom Video Communications' first-ever CIO in late 2017. He describes his 16 months in the role, highlighting Zoom's strong culture, innovative technology, and the refreshing experience of working in a digital-native organization. Moseley also shares insights on board memberships and future tech trends like AI and 5G.

title: Simplify Data Management Across Public or Private Clouds with NetApp Cloud Volumes
summary: NetApp is enhancing data management across public and private clouds by offering a feature-rich portfolio of cloud data services. The article details NetApp's public cloud offerings like Azure NetApp Files, Cloud Volumes Service for Google Cloud and AWS, and Cloud Volumes ONTAP, alongside on-premises solutions such as NetApp HCI and Cloud Volumes Service On-Premises. These solutions aim to provide enterprise-class file services, high performance, and simplified data management, catering to various cloud strategies and regulatory requirements.

title: Automatically Tier Your Data to Amazon S3 Glacier with NetApp StorageGRID
summary: NetApp StorageGRID now supports automatic tiering of data to Amazon S3 Glacier, offering customers more flexibility in managing rapidly growing unstructured data across hybrid multi-cloud environments. This integration, part of StorageGRID 11.2, allows users to leverage intelligent, policy-driven data management for cost savings and simplified archiving, ensuring data is in the right place at the right time with appropriate performance and resiliency. The update also brings additional simplicity, security enhancements like multifactor authentication, and higher performance for small object workloads.

title: Fluent acquires AdParlor, a social ad specialist previously owned by Adknowledge, for $10M
summary: Fluent, a marketing company, has acquired AdParlor, a social advertising specialist, for $10 million. AdParlor, originally a major Facebook Ads API vendor, was previously owned by AdKnowledge (now V2 Ventures). This acquisition aims to integrate AdParlor's social media advertising expertise across various platforms into Fluent's existing marketing technology stack.

title: Work on Boston’s tallest office building in 25 years has started
summary: Construction has begun on One Congress, a 600-foot-tall skyscraper in Boston, set to become the city's tallest office building in 25 years. The building, scheduled to open in 2022, will serve as the new headquarters for State Street Corp., which has leased about half of its 1 million square feet. This project is part of a larger redevelopment of the Government Center Garage area and signifies continued growth in Boston's downtown job market.

title: Alibaba and JD.Com to Combine Facial Recognition With Data in Bid for Merchant Loyalty
summary: Alibaba and JD.com are integrating facial recognition and deep customer data to enhance merchant loyalty and diversify revenue streams amidst slowing e-commerce growth in China. This "new retail" approach offers personalized marketing and operational efficiencies, benefiting brands like Bestore and Nestle, while raising questions about data management and retailer dependency.

title: Keurig Dr Pepper withdraws Peñafiel bottled water from US for high arsenic levels
summary: Keurig Dr Pepper withdrew Peñafiel spring water products from the U.S. market due to arsenic levels exceeding the FDA's 10 parts per billion limit, a problem highlighted by a Consumer Reports investigation. The company stated it has notified retailers and installed enhanced filtration systems to ensure current production meets regulatory guidelines, but faces potential lawsuits and scrutiny for the delay in withdrawal. This incident raises questions about bottled water safety and the adequacy of current federal arsenic level standards, similar to challenges faced by other food and beverage companies regarding chemical residues.

title: Crate & Barrel buys up S.F.-based home furnishings company
summary: Crate & Barrel has acquired Hudson Grace, a San Francisco-based home furnishings brand, to expand its portfolio. Hudson Grace, which has five stores in California, will continue to operate as a standalone business under the international retailer. This strategic acquisition aims to complement Crate & Barrel's existing labels.

title: FedEx slashes two-day air prices to match ground rates to fill its planes
summary: FedEx is cutting prices for two-day air service to match ground shipping rates for some customers of its Express network. This strategy aims to attract online merchants, especially as the company ends its air-shipping contract with Amazon.com Inc., and to boost its flagging Express network by filling its planes. The move comes as FedEx anticipates a doubling of daily packages shipped in the U.S. by 2026 due to the growth in online shopping.

title: Cloud Services Starting To Overtake On-Prem Database Management Systems
summary: A new report by Gartner Inc. indicates that cloud services are rapidly overtaking on-premises solutions in the database management system (DBMS) market, accounting for 68% of the market's 18.4% growth from 2017 to 2018. Gartner predicts that on-premises DBMS will become a "legacy" approach, with significant growth driven by Amazon Web Services and Microsoft's cloud offerings. The shift is attributed to factors like Software as a Service applications, pay-as-you-go pricing, and innovation primarily occurring in cloud DBMS.

title: Blockchain Could Make You—Not Equifax—the Owner of Your Data
summary: This article discusses how blockchain technology can empower individuals to own and monetize their personal data, challenging traditional data brokers like Equifax. It explains how blockchain-based solutions use cryptography, such as keys, hashes, and smart contracts, to create a decentralized system for data exchange, giving users control over who accesses and profits from their information. The piece also addresses the challenges of scalability and storage within blockchain technology but highlights its potential to disrupt the current data economy.

title: 4 Reasons the Stock Market's Outlook Is Bright: Goldman
summary: Goldman Sachs identifies four key reasons for a bullish stock market outlook, including a strong start to the year, upward earnings revisions, investor caution, and low odds of a NAFTA breakup. They also highlight that stocks with strong secular revenue growth are best positioned to outperform. The S&P 500's performance, corporate earnings growth, and specific stock recommendations are discussed.

title: Target kicks off back-to-school season with new clothes, college departments and more
summary: Target is expanding its back-to-school offerings with new uniform items under its Cat & Jack brand and launching a new '"More Than Magic" tween girl brand. The retailer is also introducing "Back to College" sections in over 700 stores near college campuses and enhancing its School List Assist service. These initiatives aim to provide a broader range of products and convenience for both K-12 and college shoppers for the upcoming season.

title: Can Adobe's Digital Experience Revenues Exceed Digital Media Revenues By 2025?
summary: This article examines whether Adobe's Digital Experience revenues can surpass Digital Media revenues by 2025, noting the former's faster growth rate. While Digital Experience is expanding rapidly, driven by market growth and strategic acquisitions, Digital Media is expected to remain the larger segment through 2025 due to its established market share and steady expansion. The analysis provides detailed forecasts and market share projections for both segments.

title: JPMorgan Chase expands Seattle engineering center to 100 people, plans to add hundreds more
summary: JPMorgan Chase is significantly expanding its technology engineering center in Seattle, growing to 100 people in its first year and signing a new lease to accommodate hundreds more. This expansion is part of the financial services giant's major investment in cloud technology, partnering with AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud, and signals Seattle's growing potential as a fintech hub. The bank's CEO, Jamie Dimon, initially skeptical, is now fully committed to cloud adoption and integrating AI into operations.

title: Expedia shows off $900M Seattle waterfront campus as thousands of employees prepare to move in
summary: Expedia showcased its new $900 million Seattle waterfront campus as thousands of employees prepare to move in. The campus, located in the Interbay neighborhood, is a sprawling space with stunning waterfront views, featuring biophilic design and a mix of renovated and new buildings. The move signifies a major shift from its former Bellevue headquarters, with the company implementing solutions to mitigate traffic impacts and aiming to house over 8,000 workers eventually.

title: Domino’s CEO Doesn’t Want a Robot Making Your Pizza
summary: Domino's CEO Ritch Allison believes pizza will endure, but acknowledges a high-tech shift in its creation and delivery. While the company is exploring innovations like driverless delivery and digital assistants for ordering, Allison expresses reservations about robots making pizzas. Domino's (DPZ) faces increasing competition from other delivery services in the quick-service restaurant industry.

title: Apple Leases 635 KSF Office Campus in Seattle
summary: Apple has signed a long-term lease with Kilroy Realty Corp. to fully occupy 333 Dexter, a 635,000-square-foot campus in Seattle’s South Lake Union. The two-tower project, Kilroy Realty's first ground-up development in the city, is scheduled for completion in late 2019. Apple plans to hire over 2,000 employees in the city within the next five years for this new location.
